rewrites.1CBD627A: The study began with a hypothesis tree: each entry named a lever on growth and was framed so the evidence could test it. The tested tree became the plan's framework of three strategic goals, six themes and twenty objectives (Figure ES.2). Appendix A1 rates the evidence behind each objective. Objective 20, on workforce and service skills, rests on a labour analysis that execution commissions first (I18).
rewrites.2B7450FF: The demand model takes international arrivals from 1,498,829 in 2025 to 1,822,634, 2,175,778 or 2,516,282 in 2035. It also marks 2025 capacity at 1.8 million inbound seats (section 2.4).
rewrites.45B63BD1: The calendar or financial basis and the source series of the 1,498,829 base are not stated, and the 2025 bars are not marked as actuals or model values. ACSA passenger arrivals (1.57 million in FY25/26), SA Tourism tourist arrivals, OAG air arrivals and model arrivals are not reconciled.[^447]
rewrites.53A05736: The report keeps the series apart under three rules. International passenger arrivals at Cape Town International, by fiscal year, are the baseline and tracking series, with FY24/25 at 1.44 million. That series counts passengers, not tourists, and Cape Town air arrivals stand proxy for the province in the market shares. The model's 2025 base of 1,498,829 and its 2035 points are the target series. What the model counts, and how its hub group is built, is still to be confirmed in writing. South African Tourism's provincial count is used, through Wesgro Research's source market analysis, to measure the province's share of global and market travel from 2022 to 2024. The model also splits markets differently from SA Tourism. Over 2022 to 2024 SA Tourism's yearly averages for India and China were a quarter to a fifth of the model's 2025 values, and France's about three times, though the periods differ. The report quotes the series side by side and never adds one to the other.[^448]
rewrites.3401488A: The model's 2025 base of 1,498,829 sits just below SA Tourism's count of 1,538,142 for 2025. Yet each market group's 2025 value tracks its 2024 value grown at the model's own rate. The report therefore treats the base as a model value until its basis is confirmed.[^450]

rewrites.04ABE854: The quarterly scorecard carries one row per indicator: code, name, baseline and year, latest value and date, direction against the path, target, source and reporting unit or data holder. The annual Board outlook adds the Tier 1 chart against both cases and the gate status. The dashboard data model lists each feed, its refresh frequency and the manual-entry form for indicators without a feed. The templates themselves are delivered with the Excel toolkit.
rewrites.79A3034D: June holds 6.4% of 2025 international seat capacity; ICCA meetings 33 to 58 from 2022 to 2024; 36 bids secured in 2024/25 at an estimated R745.1m, which are not delivered winter nights; green-season passenger traffic doubled from 2015 to 2025, while Cape Town sample occupancy in May to August 2025 stayed below 2019

rewrites.59426A0B: The assessment models tourism supply in three layers (attractions, services and infrastructure) and holds that the weakest layer constrains destination performance. Its asset database sorts the layers into twelve categories with named subtypes. It draws on Wesgro, SANParks, Stats SA and CapeNature data, with Overpass, WikiQuery and tourism reports for 2023 to 2025 named as sources of geographical data points.[^458]
rewrites.2572ABDC: Five of the six printed growth rates exceed the report's 3% to 5% norm and two clearly beat 2024's actual global growth of 11%. Four of the six cases pair structural demand creation with demand activation.
rewrites.71EB9B71: The screen scored 30 destinations on the twelve criteria and ranked them on one average score. Four of the six comparators were taken from its top ranks (section 2.2). New Zealand, ranked seventh at 3.67, and Kenya, ranked eleventh at 3.50, joined for what the score could not weigh: a remote single-gateway case and an African case with community-based tourism.[^453]
rewrites.48E8E662: The team held structured sessions with key stakeholders, extracted insights, mapped each to the study's framework of goals and objectives and aggregated them. Each insight is a concise statement written by the team, not a verbatim quotation. Every row carries a goal, a category of the framework and one impact rating of High, Medium or Low. The ratings are not defined, and no session dates, participants or roles are recorded, so this appendix attributes insights to organisations and does not quote them.[^485]
